observations.explanation: The paper describes configurable sequence length and task complexity and four categories—retrieval, multi-hop tracing, aggregation, and QA—beyond simple retrieval (PDF pp. 1–5, 15).

The authors evaluate ten models on 13 tasks and report substantial degradation as sequence length increases; they contrast this with near-perfect passkey and vanilla NIAH results (PDF pp. 6–7, 21). The appendix does show some exceptions to near-perfect vanilla NIAH, but the observation does not claim every model is perfect.

Variable tracking is described as a minimal proxy for coreference-chain resolution, and aggregation is explicitly introduced as a proxy for summarization; the paper also states that RULER consists solely of synthetic tasks (PDF pp. 1–2, 5).

Effective length is defined using the Llama2-7B 4K performance threshold (PDF p. 6). The paper reports alternative weighted-average schemes for model rankings, but does not establish how effective-length judgments change under alternative thresholds (PDF pp. 6, 14–16).
